design_notes: Deduplicated context-only survey scenarios. These are not full CI information flows because the data/output parameter is intentionally omitted.
Participant-facing items contain only context, space, sender, subject, recipient, purpose, and transmission principle.
All output/data fields are null placeholders to be supplied later when mapping system or baseline outputs.
Do not use these scenarios for ci_constraints evaluation until output_data_slot is filled.

Child-related scenarios are excluded from this version: scenarios with subject=child, school/classroom context, school monitoring sender/recipient, or child/school/classroom labels were removed from the survey pool.
Five additional non-child gray/conditionally acceptable contexts were appended after the existing scenario IDs as S033-S037; existing scenario IDs were preserved.

counts.note: This is a deduplicated context-only scenario pool. It intentionally excludes output/data fields; add those later to instantiate full CI information flows. Child-related scenarios were removed for the participant-facing survey because the child/guardian perspective caused confusion in pilot feedback. Five additional non-child, gray/conditionally acceptable contexts were appended as S033-S037 to better stress-test context-sensitive preprocessing decisions without relying on new hard-violation cases.

human_readable_glossary.description: Human-readable labels, definitions, and examples for machine CI terms used in the focused 100-flow study.

context.label: private home
context.definition: A resident’s own home or apartment.
context.example: A family home or shared apartment.

context.label: hospital or clinic
context.definition: A healthcare setting where medical care is provided.
context.example: A hospital patient room or clinic room.

context.label: long-term care home
context.definition: A residential care setting for older adults or people needing assistance.
context.example: An assisted-living facility.

context.label: public area
context.definition: A place generally open to the public.
context.example: A public walkway or entrance area.

context.label: research smart-home lab
context.definition: A living space used for research studies.
context.example: A smart apartment used in a university study.

context.label: short-term rental
context.definition: A temporary rental property controlled by a host.
context.example: An Airbnb or Vrbo stay.

context.label: workplace
context.definition: A place where employees work.
context.example: An office, shop, or company building.

purpose.label: clinical care
purpose.definition: Supporting medical care or patient monitoring.
purpose.example: Patient monitoring by clinicians.

purpose.label: voice command or communication
purpose.definition: Responding to speech commands or communication-related events.
purpose.example: Recognizing a smart speaker command.

purpose.label: energy or lighting automation
purpose.definition: Adjusting HVAC, lighting, or energy use.
purpose.example: Turning lights on/off based on occupancy.

purpose.label: fall detection
purpose.definition: Detecting whether a person has fallen.
purpose.example: Sending a fall alert to a caregiver.

purpose.label: personalization
purpose.definition: Adapting a service to a person’s routine or preferences.
purpose.example: Learning daily activity patterns for automation.

purpose.label: research study
purpose.definition: Collecting information for a research study.
purpose.example: Studying activity in a smart-home lab.

purpose.label: routine monitoring
purpose.definition: Monitoring everyday activities or routines over time.
purpose.example: Tracking cooking, sleeping, or room-use patterns.

purpose.label: safety monitoring
purpose.definition: Detecting safety-relevant events.
purpose.example: Detecting a fall, alarm, or dangerous sound.

purpose.label: security monitoring
purpose.definition: Detecting visitors, intrusions, or safety/security events.
purpose.example: Notifying a homeowner that someone is at the door.

purpose.label: training or supervision
purpose.definition: Using the information for instruction, supervision, or training.
purpose.example: School staff reviewing classroom behavior.

purpose.label: work performance monitoring
purpose.definition: Monitoring employee activity or work patterns.
purpose.example: Tracking whether employees are present or active.

recipient.label: authorized staff
recipient.definition: Staff who are officially allowed to access the information.

recipient.label: caregiver
recipient.definition: A person responsible for helping or caring for the subject.

recipient.label: clinician
recipient.definition: A healthcare professional.
recipient.example: Doctor, nurse, or care team member.

recipient.label: the app or software service
recipient.definition: The app or software service that would receive the listed output to perform the task.
recipient.example: An HVAC app, fall-detection app, or sound-monitoring service.

recipient.label: homeowner/resident
recipient.definition: The person who owns or manages their own home system.

recipient.label: rental host
recipient.definition: The owner or manager of a short-term rental.

recipient.label: researcher
recipient.definition: A person conducting a study.

sender.label: organization-operated system
sender.definition: The organization responsible for deciding how the data is collected and used.
sender.example: An employer-operated workplace monitoring system.

sender.label: hospital monitoring system
sender.definition: A system operated by a hospital or clinic.
sender.example: A camera or sensor used by hospital staff.

sender.label: rental host’s device
sender.definition: A device controlled by the rental host or property owner.
sender.example: A camera or sensor installed by an Airbnb/Vrbo host.

sender.label: resident-owned device
sender.definition: A device controlled by the homeowner or resident.
sender.example: A smart doorbell or home camera owned by the resident.

sender.label: patient/family device
sender.definition: A device installed or managed by a patient or family member.
sender.example: A fall detector installed by an older adult’s family.

sender.label: research sensor system
sender.definition: A sensor system operated by researchers.
sender.example: Sensors in a university living-lab study.

space.label: bedroom
space.definition: Room used for sleeping or private activities.

space.label: living room
space.example: Living room in a home or rental.

space.label: outdoor area
space.definition: An exterior area outside the building.

space.label: patient room
space.definition: Private or semi-private room for clinical care.

space.label: work area
space.example: Desk area, office, or shared workspace.

subject.label: employee
subject.definition: A person working for an organization.
subject.example: Worker in an office or company facility.

subject.label: guest
subject.definition: A temporary guest or rental guest.
subject.example: A party guest or short-term-rental guest.

subject.label: patient
subject.definition: A person receiving medical care.
subject.example: Hospital or clinic patient.

subject.label: research participant
subject.definition: A person enrolled in a research study.
subject.example: Participant in a smart-home living-lab study.

subject.label: resident
subject.definition: A person who lives in the space.
subject.example: Home resident or care-home resident.

subject.label: roommate
subject.definition: A co-resident sharing the home.
subject.example: Housemate in a shared apartment.

subject.label: visitor
subject.definition: A person visiting the space.
subject.example: Someone at the door or visiting a home.

transmission_principle.label: only authorized people can access it
transmission_principle.definition: Access is limited to approved people.
transmission_principle.example: Only approved care staff can see the alert.

transmission_principle.label: sent to a cloud service
transmission_principle.definition: The information is processed by a remote cloud service.
transmission_principle.example: Audio or video sent to a vendor cloud.

transmission_principle.label: ongoing/continuous monitoring
transmission_principle.definition: The system collects or shares information on an ongoing basis rather than only for a single event.
transmission_principle.example: Always-on monitoring throughout the day.

transmission_principle.label: people nearby are told monitoring is happening
transmission_principle.definition: People nearby are told that the sensing or sharing is happening, such as through a sign, notice, or setup screen.
transmission_principle.example: A sign, notice, or setup screen explains the sensor.

transmission_principle.label: only when an event occurs
transmission_principle.definition: The system shares information only after a relevant event is detected.
transmission_principle.example: Only sends a door alert when someone appears.

transmission_principle.label: explicit consent is obtained
transmission_principle.definition: The person has explicitly agreed to the data sharing.
transmission_principle.example: A signed consent form or clear opt-in.

transmission_principle.label: not disclosed to the person being monitored
transmission_principle.definition: The person being monitored is not told that the device or data sharing is happening.
transmission_principle.example: A hidden rental camera or sensor.

transmission_principle.label: disclosed in the rental listing
transmission_principle.definition: The device and coverage must be described in the rental listing.
transmission_principle.example: The listing says an outdoor camera covers the entrance.

transmission_principle.label: processed on the device or local hub
transmission_principle.definition: Information is analyzed on the local device or local hub rather than sent to a cloud service for processing. The listed output may still be shared with the stated recipient.
transmission_principle.example: A local device or home hub detects an event before any listed output is shared.

transmission_principle.label: speech content is removed before sharing
transmission_principle.definition: Spoken words or conversation content are removed before the output is shared; non-speech sounds may remain.
transmission_principle.example: Only non-speech sounds, a noise label, or a decibel level is shared.

transmission_principle.label: written notice is provided to affected people
transmission_principle.definition: People affected by the monitoring receive written notice.
transmission_principle.example: A written workplace, care or study notice.
